record.title: The 2–3 conjecture for a transcendence basis of multiple zeta values
record.statement:
Let $\zeta(s_1,\ldots,s_k)$ denote a multiple zeta value of weight $s_1+\cdots+s_k$. A word in the alphabet $\{2,3\}$ is called Lyndon when it is strictly smaller than each of its proper nontrivial suffixes in the chosen lexicographic order. **The 2–3 conjecture.** The set

$$
\left\{\zeta(s_1,\ldots,s_k): k\ge1,\ s_j\in\{2,3\},\ \text{$s_1\cdots s_k$ is a Lyndon word}\right\}
$$

gives a transcendence basis of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra of multiple zeta values. This conjecture would determine the transcendence degree in each weight and gives a concrete proposed basis indexed by Lyndon words on $\{2,3\}$. The supplied source gives no evidence of a resolution, so its status is left open.
record.source_name: German Combariza, “A few conjectures about the multiple zeta values”, arXiv:1207.1735 (2012).

record.title: Infinite generation and odd-degree generators of the symplectic commutative graph algebra
record.statement:
Let $H_*(\mathfrak{c}^+_\infty)^{\mathrm{Sp}}$ be the symplectic-invariant homology algebra, let $\mathcal{A}^+(\phi)$ be the subalgebra generated by the positive-degree elements of $\mathcal{A}(\phi)$, and let

$$
\mathcal{E}=H_*(\mathfrak{c}^+_\infty)^{\mathrm{Sp}}/\mathcal{I}(\mathcal{A}^+(\phi))
$$

be the resulting free graded commutative algebra. **The conjecture.** The free graded algebra $\mathcal{E}$ is infinitely generated, and there exist infinitely many generators with odd degrees. The preceding results identify the initial low-weight pieces of $\mathcal{E}$, but do not determine its full generating set; the asserted infinite generation and odd-degree phenomenon remain open.

record.title: Kühnel and Lutz's tightness conjecture on strong minimality
record.statement: Let $X$ be a simplicial complex. Call $X$ **$\mathbb{F}$-tight** when it has the tightness property over a field $\mathbb{F}$, and call it **strongly minimal** when it achieves the componentwise smallest face vector among all triangulations of its geometric carrier $|X|$. **Kühnel and Lutz's tightness conjecture.** Every $\mathbb{F}$-tight simplicial complex is strongly minimal. If true, this would strengthen ordinary minimality by asserting that tight triangulations minimize every face-number component among triangulations of the same carrier; the source presents it as an open conjecture.

record.title: Broadhurst's third-category conjecture for flat ternary cyclotomic polynomials
record.statement:
Let $p<q<r$ be odd primes, let $A(pqr)$ denote the height of $\Phi_{pqr}(x)$, and let $w$ be the smallest positive integer such that

$$
r\equiv\pm w\pmod{pq}.
$$
 **Broadhurst's third-category conjecture.** Suppose that $A(pqr)=1$ and $p\not\equiv1\pmod w$. Then

$$
w>p,\qquad q>p^2-p,\qquad q\equiv\pm1\pmod p,\qquad w\equiv\pm1\pmod p.
$$
 Moreover, if $w\equiv1\pmod p$, then $q\not\equiv\pm1\pmod{wp}$. This is presented as part of Broadhurst's third category of flat ternary cyclotomic polynomials. The source notes that the converse is false, so the asserted necessary conditions remain the open content.
record.source_name: Sam Elder, “Flat Cyclotomic Polynomials: A New Approach”, arXiv:1207.5811 (2012).

record.title: Broadhurst's third-category conjecture for pseudocyclotomic ternary polynomials
record.statement:
Let $p<q<r$ be relatively prime positive integers, let $\widetilde\Phi_{p,q,r}(x)$ be flat, and let $w$ be the smallest positive integer such that

$$
r\equiv\pm w\pmod{pq}.
$$
 **Pseudocyclotomic third-category conjecture.** Suppose that $p\not\equiv1\pmod w$. Then

$$
w>p,\qquad q>p^2-p,\qquad q\equiv\pm1\pmod p,\qquad w\equiv\pm1\pmod p.
$$
 Moreover, if $w\equiv1\pmod p$, then $q\not\equiv1\pmod{wp}$. The paper says that this and the preceding pseudocyclotomic conjecture appear to hold from limited data, but provides no proof.

record.title: Entropy criterion for birational maps from cluster recurrences
record.statement:
Let $b_{1,j+1}$ be the coefficients defining a birational map $$ corresponding to a recurrence $$, and let $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. Define

$$
P_{\pm}(\lambda)=\lambda^N+1-\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}[\pm b_{1,j+1}]_+\lambda^j.
$$

Let $\lambda_{\max}$ be the root of largest magnitude among the roots of these two polynomials. **Entropy criterion conjecture.** The algebraic entropy is $\mathcal{E}=\log|\lambda_{\max}|$, and it is positive if and only if

$$
\max\left(\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}[b_{1,j+1}]_+,\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}[-b_{1,j+1}]_+\right)\geq3.
$$

This would give an explicit test for exponential degree growth and distinguish positive-entropy recurrences from zero-entropy cases; its general validity is presented as the main conjecture and remains open.
record.source_name: Allan Fordy and Andrew Hone, “Discrete integrable systems and Poisson algebras from cluster maps”, arXiv:1207.6072 (2012).

record.title: Zhang–Liu–Wang conjecture on the adjacent vertex distinguishing chromatic index
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with no isolated vertices. Write $V(G)$ and $E(G)$ for its vertex and edge sets, let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, and let $\chi'_{a}(G)$ denote the smallest number of colors in an adjacent vertex distinguishing edge coloring of $G$. A graph is **normal** if it contains no isolated edges. **Zhang–Liu–Wang's conjecture.** If $G$ is a connected normal graph different from a $5$-cycle and satisfies $|V(G)|\geqslant 3$, then

$$
\chi'_{a}(G)\leqslant\Delta(G)+2.
$$

The conjecture concerns an upper bound for the adjacent vertex distinguishing chromatic index in terms of maximum degree. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: Smooth splitting conjecture for the twisted bundle over Hitchin's moduli space
record.statement:
Let $V_z$ be the twisted bundle obtained as the globally defined direct sum of the two locally defined bundles $V_z^1$ and $V_z^2$ over the relevant cover of the Hitchin moduli space. **Smooth splitting conjecture.** The twisted bundle $V_z$ admits a $C^{\infty}$ splitting

$$
V_z=V_z^1\oplus V_z^2.
$$

Such a splitting would globalize the two sheet-dependent summands and is needed to construct the corresponding hyperholomorphic connection; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: The square-root grid general position subset conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f(n,\ell)$ denote the largest guaranteed size of a subset in general position among every set of $n$ points in the plane with at most $\ell$ collinear. The $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ grid is a point set in the plane with at most $\sqrt{n}$ collinear. **Square-root grid conjecture.**

$$
f(n,\sqrt{n}) \geqslant \Omega(\sqrt{n}).
$$

This conjecture would completely answer Gowers' question by showing that $\operatorname{GP}(q)=\Theta(q^2)$. It is true for the $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ grid.

record.title: The fixed-collinearity general position subset conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f(n,\ell)$ be the largest guaranteed size of a subset in general position among every set of $n$ points in the plane with at most $\ell$ collinear, and let $\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ denote a fixed polylogarithmic factor in $n$. **Fixed-collinearity subset conjecture.** If $\ell$ is fixed, then

$$
f(n,\ell) \geqslant \Omega_{\ell}\left(\frac{n}{\operatorname{polylog}(n)}\right).
$$

Determining the correct asymptotics of $f(n,\ell)$ for fixed $\ell$ remains wide open. Existing lower bounds are essentially combinatorial, since the Szemerédi–Trotter theorem gives little information for point sets with bounded collinearities.

record.title: The eventual junction-occupation conjecture for all local-maximal polygon fillings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be the polygonal domain under consideration and let $M(G)$ be its medial axis, including its junction points. A **filling solution that is a local maximum** is a filling by $N$ discs whose filling measure is locally maximal.

**Eventual all-local-maxima junction-occupation conjecture.** For a given $G$ and $M(G)$, there is an $N'$ such that for $N\geq N'$, the junction points are always occupied in all filling solutions that are local maxima.

This is explicitly proposed as a stronger version of the conjecture for optimal filling solutions, and would ensure that every sufficiently large local maximum occupies all junction points. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution status.

record.title: The topological-surface asymptotic bondage-number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of orientable genus $h$ and non-orientable genus $k$. Let $b(G)$ be its bondage number and $\Delta(G)$ its maximum vertex degree. Let $c_h$ and $c'_k$ be constants depending, respectively, on the orientable and non-orientable genera of $G$, and let $o(h)$ and $o(k)$ denote the genus-dependent terms appearing in the conjecture. **Topological-surface bondage-number conjecture.**

$$
b(G)\le\min\{c_h,\,c'_k,\,\Delta(G)+o(h),\,\Delta(G)+o(k)\}.
$$

The conjecture proposes that refinements of the paper's surface-embedding arguments yield both constant and maximum-degree-based upper bounds across topological surfaces. The paper presents it as a general conjectural direction after proving explicit bounds, but no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Gyárfás–Sárközy–Selkow conjecture on multicolored matchings in uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $K_n^r$ be the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. A **$t$-edge-coloring** assigns one of $t$ colors to each edge, and an **$s$-colored matching** is a matching whose edges use at most $s$ colors, where $1\leq s\leq t$.

**Gyárfás–Sárközy–Selkow conjecture.** Every $t$-coloring of the edges of $K_n^r$ contains an $s$-colored matching of size $k$ provided that

$$
n\geq kr+\left\lfloor{\frac{\left(k-1\right)\left(t-s\right)}{1+r+r^2+\cdots r^{s-1}}}\right\rfloor.
$$

The case $s=1$ is the Alon–Frankl–Lovász theorem, while the case $s=t$ is trivial. The conjecture extends monochromatic matching Ramsey results to matchings using several colors; the source singles out the case $t=3$, $s=2$, whose smallest nontrivial instance is proved there for $r=3$ and $k=4$.

record.title: Regularity conjecture for critical graphs at maximum degree eight
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a critical graph, meaning that deleting any vertex lowers its chromatic number, with chromatic number $\chi$ and maximum degree $\Delta$. **Regularity conjecture.** Every critical graph with

$$
\chi \geq \Delta = 8
$$

is regular.

The conjecture is motivated by the absence of known critical, or connected even, counterexamples to the Borodin–Kostochka conjecture for $\Delta=8$ other than a regular example. Its status is left unresolved in the source.

record.title: The Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits spectral-gap conjecture
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a centered log-concave random vector in $\mathbb R^n$, let $\lambda_X^2$ be the largest eigenvalue of its covariance matrix, and let $g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be locally Lipschitz. **The Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $C$ such that

$$
\operatorname{Var}g(X)\leq C\lambda_X^2\mathbb E|\nabla g(X)|^2.
$$

This is a spectral-gap conjecture for log-concave probability measures and implies the variance conjecture by taking $X$ isotropic and $g(X)=|X|^2$. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The general variance conjecture for centered log-concave vectors
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a centered log-concave random vector in $\mathbb R^n$, let $\lambda_X^2$ denote the largest eigenvalue of its covariance matrix, and let $|X|$ be its Euclidean norm. **The general variance conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $C$ such that

$$
\operatorname{Var}|X|^2\leq C\lambda_X^2\mathbb E|X|^2.
$$

This is the non-isotropic specialization of the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture with $g(X)=|X|^2$. The paper studies this conjecture and states that it is equivalent to a general thin-shell width conjecture.

record.title: Boundary Colin de Verdière conjecture for the first Steklov eigenvalue
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a compact surface with boundary, and let $\sigma_1(M)$ denote its first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue. Define $\mathrm{Chr}(M,\partial M)$ to be the number of vertices of the largest complete graph that can be embedded in $M$ with all vertices on $\partial M$. **Boundary Colin de Verdière conjecture.** The maximal multiplicity of $\sigma_1(M)$ is

$$
\mathrm{Chr}(M,\partial M)-1.
$$
 This conjecture is a Steklov analogue of Colin de Verdière's conjecture for Schrödinger operators on surfaces, replacing the chromatic number by a boundary-embedded graph invariant. The supplied source does not report a resolution.

record.title: Geometric limit conjecture for the largest family sizes in the critical case
record.statement:
Let $Z_p$ be a critical clonal process in a general supercritical splitting tree, with finite second moment

$$
\sigma^2:=\int_0^\infty \Lambda(\mathrm{d}u)u^2
$$

and let $r$ denote the Malthusian growth rate. Define

$$
x_t:=\frac{2}{\sigma^2}(rt^2-t\log t).
$$

**Geometric limit conjecture.** As $t\to\infty$, on the survival event, $L_t(x_t)$ converges in distribution to a non-degenerate geometric random variable.
This conjecture concerns the still-open problem of determining the order of magnitude and limiting behaviour of the largest families in the critical case; the surrounding discussion notes that analogous results are known under additional assumptions, but the size problem itself remains open.

record.title: The coisotropic orbit characterization for symplectic representations
record.statement:
Let $({\mathfrak m},V,\omega)$ be a symplectic representation of the Lie algebra ${\mathfrak m}$. A subspace $W\subseteq V$ is coisotropic when $W^{\perp_\omega}\subseteq W$, where $W^{\perp_\omega}=\{v\in V:\omega(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\in W\}$. An ${\mathfrak m}$-equivariant symmetric bilinear map is a symmetric bilinear map compatible with the ${\mathfrak m}$-actions on $V$ and ${\mathfrak m}$. **Coisotropic orbit characterization.** The subspace ${\mathfrak m}\cdot A$ is coisotropic for all nonzero $A\in V$ if and only if there exists an ${\mathfrak m}$-equivariant symmetric bilinear map

$$
B_{\mu}:V\times V\rightarrow {\mathfrak m}
$$

which satisfies the identity referred to in the source as. This would characterize symplectic representations whose nonzero infinitesimal orbits are all coisotropic by the existence of the additional bilinear map. The preceding theorem proves that the coisotropy condition holds for special symplectic representations, but the converse characterization is presented as a conjecture and its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Conjecture on partial symmetries in dimension three
record.statement: Let ${\mathfrak D}$ denote the set of block-positive symmetries under consideration, and let $s\in{\mathfrak D}$ be a partial symmetry for $n=3$. **Partial-symmetry conjecture.** The rank of $s^2$ is equal to $5$, and $s$ corresponds to a decomposable positive map. The preceding examples exhibit partial symmetries of rank $5$ whose corresponding maps are decomposable, while no example with rank $7$ or with a non-decomposable corresponding map was found; the conjecture asserts that these possibilities never occur.

record.title: Conference-matrix MDS code conjecture
record.statement: Let $p$ be a prime, and let ${\mathbb C}$ be a code of length $p+1$ constructed from a generator matrix that is a conference matrix. **Conference-matrix MDS conjecture.** The code ${\mathbb C}$ is an MDS code of dimension $\frac{p+1}{2}$ and minimum Hamming distance $\frac{p+3}{2}$. This would give an MDS code with parameters determined by the rank of a conference matrix over ${\mathbb Z}_p$; the source provides no resolution of the claim.

record.title: Wilfong–Haxell–Winkler delay-colouring conjecture for bipartite multigraphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a bipartite multigraph with partition classes $A,B$ and maximum degree $d$. Each edge $e$ has an associated integer delay $r(e)$. An edge-colouring is a map $f:E(G)\to\{0,\ldots,d\}$, and $f+r\pmod{d+1}$ is defined on an edge $e$ as $f(e)+r(e)\pmod{d+1}$. **Wilfong–Haxell–Winkler's delay-colouring conjecture.** The graph $G$ admits an edge-colouring $f$ such that $f$ is proper on $A$ and $f+r\pmod{d+1}$ is proper on $B$. This conjecture is motivated by scheduling in optical networks and is proved in the paper in the special case $d=3$; the general case remains open.

record.title: Nash-Williams's regular-subgraph conjecture for Hamilton-cycle packings
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $\operatorname{reg}_{\operatorname{even}}(G)$ be the largest degree of an even-regular spanning subgraph of $G$. For integers $n$ and $\delta$, define

$$
\operatorname{reg}_{\operatorname{even}}(n,\delta):=\min\{\operatorname{reg}_{\operatorname{even}}(G): |G|=n,\ \delta(G)=\delta\}.
$$

**Nash-Williams's conjecture.** If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree $\delta\ge n/2$, then $G$ contains at least

$$
\frac{\operatorname{reg}_{\operatorname{even}}(n,\delta)}{2}
$$

edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles. This is the natural optimal bound based on the largest guaranteed even-regular spanning subgraph; the paper presents it as an open problem in general.

record.title: The regular-subgraph conjecture for Hamilton-cycle packings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{reg}_{\operatorname{even}}(G)$ denote the largest degree of an even-regular spanning subgraph of $G$. **The regular-subgraph conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)\ge \frac{n}{2},
$$

then $G$ contains at least

$$
\frac{\operatorname{reg}_{\operatorname{even}}(G)}{2}
$$

edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles. This graph-by-graph strengthening of the preceding conjecture is best possible for each individual graph. It was proved when $\delta\ge(2-\sqrt{2}+\varepsilon)n$, but remains open in general.

record.title: Maximum genus range of assembly graphs with an even number of vertices
record.statement:
For an assembly graph with $n$ vertices, let its genus range be the set of genera of its associated ribbon graphs. Let $[a,b]$ denote the integer interval $\{a,a+1,\ldots,b\}$.

**Maximum-genus-range conjecture.** The maximum genus range of assembly graphs with $2n$ vertices is

$$
[n-1,n]
$$

for any $n\in\mathbb N$.

The preceding theorem determines the genus range of tangled cords, and the source states this even-vertex assertion as a conjecture. No resolution evidence is supplied.

record.title: Kadec–Pełczyński dichotomy for preduals of JBW*-triples
record.statement:
Let $W$ be a JBW$^*$-triple and let $(\phi_n)$ be a bounded sequence of functionals in its predual. A **tripotent** is an element of $W$ satisfying the defining tripotent identity, and two tripotents are mutually orthogonal when they are orthogonal in the JBW$^*$-triple sense. For $e\in W$, let $P_2(e)$ denote the Peirce-2 projection associated with $e$.

**Kadec–Pełczyński dichotomy conjecture.** There exist a subsequence $(\phi_{\tau(n)})$ and a sequence of mutually orthogonal tripotents $(e_n)$ in $W$ such that

$$
\left\\{\phi_{\tau(n)}-\phi_{\tau(n)}P_2(e_n):n\in\mathbb N\right\\}
$$

is relatively weakly compact, and, for every $n$,

$$
\phi_{\tau(n)}=\xi_n+\psi_n,\qquad \xi_n:=\phi_{\tau(n)}-\phi_{\tau(n)}P_2(e_n),\qquad \psi_n:=\phi_{\tau(n)}P_2(e_n).
$$

This would extend the Kadec–Pełczyński dichotomy from JBW$^*$-algebra preduals to the more general setting of JBW$^*$-triple preduals; the absence of a positive cone is precisely the obstacle identified in the source, and the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Francisco J. FernÁndez-Polo, Antonio M. Peralta and MarÍa Isabel RamÍrez, “A Kadec-Pelczyński dichotomy-type theorem for preduals of JBW*-algebras”, arXiv:1211.4990 (2012).

record.title: Liu–Wang–Zhang's conjecture on the neighbourhood distinguishing index
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, and let $\operatorname{ndi}(G)$ be the smallest number of colours in a proper edge colouring for which adjacent vertices receive distinct sets of colours on their incident edges.

**Liu–Wang–Zhang's conjecture.** If $G\notin\{K_2,C_5\}$, then

$$
\Delta(G)\leq \operatorname{ndi}(G)\leq \Delta(G)+2.
$$

The lower bound is immediate, while the upper bound is known for bipartite graphs and graphs with maximum degree at most three, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Ben Seamone, “The 1-2-3 Conjecture and related problems: a survey”, arXiv:1211.5122 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.5122

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2012). “The second conjecture was answered in the affirmative by Bazgan et al. .”

record.title: Baril–Togni's multigraph neighbourhood distinguishing conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected multigraph. Write $\mu(G)$ for its edge multiplicity, $\Delta(G)$ for its maximum degree, and $\operatorname{ndi}(G)$ for the neighbourhood distinguishing index.

**Baril–Togni's conjecture.** If $G\neq C_5$, then

$$
\operatorname{ndi}(G)\leq \Delta(G)+\mu(G)+1.
$$

This extends the neighbourhood distinguishing index conjecture from simple graphs to multigraphs. The source presents it as an open strengthening.
record.source_name: Ben Seamone, “The 1-2-3 Conjecture and related problems: a survey”, arXiv:1211.5122 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.5122

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2012). “The second conjecture was answered in the affirmative by Bazgan et al. .”

record.title: Bača–Jendrol'–Miller–Ryan's total edge irregularity strength conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\Delta(G)$ be its maximum degree, and let $|E(G)|$ denote its number of edges. The total edge irregularity strength $\operatorname{s}'_\Sigma{}^t(G)$ is the least $k$ for which a total $k$-weighting gives distinct values to all edges when each edge value is the sum of the weights on its endpoints and on the edge itself.

**Bača–Jendrol'–Miller–Ryan's conjecture.** If $G\not\cong K_5$, then

$$
\operatorname{s}'_\Sigma{}^t(G)=\max\left\{\left\lceil\frac{\Delta(G)+1}{2}\right\rceil,\left\lceil\frac{|E(G)|+2}{3}\right\rceil\right\}.
$$

The source reports substantial partial verification, including sufficiently dense graphs and several sparse classes, but not a complete proof.
record.source_name: Ben Seamone, “The 1-2-3 Conjecture and related problems: a survey”, arXiv:1211.5122 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.5122

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2012). “The second conjecture was answered in the affirmative by Bazgan et al. .”

record.title: Equality of finite- and countable-support discrepancy maxima
record.statement:
For a probability distribution ${\bf p}$ with finite support, let $C_n$ be the maximum of $D({\bf p})$ over distributions whose support has size $n$, and set

$$
C_\infty:=\sup_n C_n.
$$

Let

$$
C:=\max_{{\bf p}\in\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{Z}_+}}D({\bf p}).
$$

**Support-maximization conjecture.** The global maximum exists, equals the supremum of the finite-support maxima, and is strictly less than $1$:

$$
C_\infty=C<1.
$$

The paper presents this as a conjecture about the largest possible discrepancy and does not prove either the equality or the strict bound.
record.source_name: Richard Arratia and Stephen DeSalvo, “On the Random Sampling of Pairs, with Pedestrian examples”, arXiv:1211.6486 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.6486

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

record.title: Exceptional-graph conjecture for fractional powers
record.statement:
For positive integers $m,n$ with $1<m<n$, let $G^{\frac{m}{n}}$ be the $m$th power of the $n$-subdivision of a graph $G$, and let $\chi$ and $\omega$ denote its chromatic and clique numbers. **Exceptional-graph conjecture.** The conjecture that

$$
\chi\left(G^{\frac{m}{n}}\right)=\omega\left(G^{\frac{m}{n}}\right)
$$

holds for connected graphs of maximum degree at least $3$ holds except when $G=C_3\square K_2$. The paper reports proofs for several classes, including complete graphs and infinitely many values of $n$ when $m$ is odd, but the supplied text does not resolve the remaining general case.
record.source_name: Stephen Hartke, Hong Liu and Šárka Petříčková, “On coloring of fractional powers of graphs”, arXiv:1212.3898 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.3898

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2012).

record.title: Nonsingularity conjecture for the Riccati-derived M-matrices
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a regular singular $M$-matrix and let $u_1,u_2,v_1,v_2$ be the vectors associated with $K$ as in the source. The scalar products $u_1^Tv_1$ and $u_2^Tv_2$ compare the corresponding left and right null vectors. **Nonsingularity conjecture.** If

$$
u_1^Tv_1\ne u_2^Tv_2,
$$

then $I_m-Phi\Psi$ and $I_n-Psi\Phi$ are nonsingular $M$-matrices. This conjecture concerns the reducible case of algebraic Riccati equations associated with $M$-matrices; the supplied status evidence is internally inconsistent, describing failed attempts to find counterexamples while saying the conjecture is believed to be true.
record.source_name: Chun-Hua Guo, “On algebraic Riccati equations associated with M-Matrices”, arXiv:1212.6461 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.6461

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2012). “Attempts to find counterexamples for the reducible case have failed and we are led to believe that the conjecture is true.”

record.title: Bollobás and Erdős's conjecture on properly colored Hamiltonian cycles
record.statement:
Let $K_n^c$ be an edge-colored complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\Delta^{\mathrm{mon}}(K_n^c)$ be the maximum number of edges of the same color incident with a vertex of $K_n^c$. A cycle is **properly colored** if consecutive edges on the cycle have distinct colors. **Bollobás and Erdős's conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta^{\mathrm{mon}}(K_n^c)<\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor,
$$

then $K_n^c$ has a properly colored Hamiltonian cycle. This conjecture seeks a sharp maximum-monochromatic-degree condition guaranteeing a properly colored Hamiltonian cycle; the surrounding discussion records the known $7n/8$ minimum-color-degree condition and constructions showing that the weaker condition $\delta^c(K_n^c)=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ does not suffice.
record.source_name: Guanghui Wang, Tao Wang and Guizhen Liu, “Long properly colored cycles in edge colored complete graphs”, arXiv:1301.0450 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0450

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Clozel's formula for higher homology of reductive p-adic groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a reductive $p$-adic group. Choose a minimal parabolic subgroup $P_0\subset G$ with Levi decomposition $P_0=L_0U_0$. For each parabolic subgroup $P\supset P_0$ with Levi decomposition $P=LU$ and $L_0\subset L$, write $L\leq G$, let $\operatorname{r}^G_L$ be Jacquet restriction along $P$, and let $\overline{\operatorname{i}}_L^G$ be parabolic induction along the opposite parabolic. Let $\chi_L:L\to\{0,1\}$ be Clozel's characteristic function, let $L_{cz}$ be the union of the compact-mod-centre subgroups of $L$, and let $1_{L_{cz}}$ be its characteristic function. **Clozel's higher-homology conjecture.** The following is an equality of operators on $\operatorname{H}(\operatorname{H}(G))$:

$$
\sum_{L\leq G} \overline{\operatorname{i}}_L^G 1_{L_{cz}}\chi_L \operatorname{r}^G_L=1.
$$

This generalizes Clozel's formula from degree zero to higher homology. The formula is proved in the paper for $G=\operatorname{SL}_2(F)$, while the asserted identity for all reductive $p$-adic groups remains open.
record.source_name: Tyrone Crisp, “Restriction to compact subgroups in the cyclic homology of reductive p-adic groups”, arXiv:1301.0487 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0487

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Brignall's prime bound conjecture for graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $|V(G)|\geq 2$. The **prime bound** $p(G)$ is the smallest integer such that $G$ admits a prime $p(G)$-extension; here $\alpha(G)$ denotes the stability number and $\omega(G)$ the clique number. **Brignall's prime bound conjecture.**

$$
p(G)\leq\left\lceil\log_2\bigl(\max(\alpha(G),\omega(G))+1\bigr)\right\rceil.
$$

This would improve the general upper bound obtained from the number of vertices by replacing $|V(G)|$ with the larger of the stability and clique numbers. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Abderrahim Boussaïri and Pierre Ille, “Determination of the prime bound of a graph”, arXiv:1301.1157 (2013).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2013). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1110.2935](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.2935).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.1157

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Narkiewicz's conjecture on the first Narkiewicz constant
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group written as a sum of invariant factors

$$
G=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r C_{n_i},
$$

where $n_i\mid n_j$ if $i\leq j$ and $n_1>1$. Let $N_1(G)$ denote the maximum length of a unique factorization indexed multiset over $G\setminus\{0\}$. **Narkiewicz's conjecture.**

$$
N_1(G)=\sum_{i=1}^r n_i.
$$

The conjecture gives an explicit formula for the first Narkiewicz constant. The paper says that a resolution still seems far away, although the formula is known for cyclic groups, elementary $2$- and $3$-groups, and groups of the form $C_p^2$.
record.source_name: Daniel Kriz, “On the maximal cross number of unique factorization indexed multisets”, arXiv:1301.1401 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.1401

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Conjecture on consecutive-layer extremal families avoiding a fixed poset
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a fixed finite poset, let $e(P)$ be the largest integer $k$ such that the union of the $k$ middle layers of the Boolean lattice is $P$-free, and let $\operatorname{La}^c(n,P)$ be the maximum size of a $P$-free family contained in $e(P)+1$ consecutive layers. If the limit exists, define

$$
\pi^c(P)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{La}^c(n,P)}{\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}}.
$$

**Consecutive-layer conjecture.** For any fixed poset $P$,

$$
\pi^c(P)=e(P).
$$

This is presented as a weaker version of the general extremal-poset conjecture. The source highlights the diamond poset as an important unresolved case of the stronger conjecture.
record.source_name: Travis Johnston and Linyuan Lu, “Turan Problems on Non-uniform Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1301.1870 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.1870

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

record.title: Polynomial Alon–Saks–Seymour conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Its **bipartite packing** $\mathbf{bp}(G)$ is the minimum number of edge-disjoint complete bipartite graphs needed to partition the edges of $G$, and $\chi(G)$ is its chromatic number. **Polynomial Alon–Saks–Seymour conjecture.** There exists a polynomial $P$ such that

$$
\chi(G)\leq P(\mathbf{bp}(G)).
$$

The linear Alon–Saks–Seymour conjecture is false, but the existence of a polynomial bound is stated to remain open. This formulation is also presented as equivalent to the Clique–Stable Set separation conjecture.
record.source_name: Nicolas Bousquet, Aurélie Lagoutte and Stéphan Thomassé, “Clique versus Independent Set”, arXiv:1301.2474 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.2474

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2013). “Huang and Sudakov proposed in a counterexample to the Alon-Saks-Seyour conjecture (then generalized in ), twenty-five years after its statement.”

record.title: Oriented Alon–Saks–Seymour conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Its **oriented bipartite packing** $\mathbf{bp}_{\mathrm{or}}(G)$ is the minimum number of oriented complete bipartite graphs such that every edge is covered by an arc in at least one direction and by no more than one arc in the same direction. Let $\chi(G)$ denote the chromatic number. **Oriented Alon–Saks–Seymour conjecture.** There exists a polynomial $P$ such that

$$
\chi(G)\leq P(\mathbf{bp}_{\mathrm{or}}(G)).
$$

The source introduces this as a variant that may yield a superlinear lower bound for Clique–Stable Set separation. No resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Nicolas Bousquet, Aurélie Lagoutte and Stéphan Thomassé, “Clique versus Independent Set”, arXiv:1301.2474 (2014).
